experiments.assessment: Rejected against 2.90. Holding a recently sheltered position or diverting toward it can interfere with pressure or subsequent movement. The official 48-match aggregate does not identify the cause. Retain fire discipline and test quiet field-of-view scanning next.

experiments.hypothesis: Route around walls that block urgent ground travel to the circle. Bounded A* runs across decisions. Following a verified detour permits temporary movement away from the circle while already outside; inside the current zone its border still applies.

experiments.assessment: Selected by the official site. Against the 2.65 policy, this experiment raised the 48-match mean by 0.25. Changes to received damage, elimination count and individual placements are not exposed. Rebuild early-route and shelter experiments on this selected source.

experiments.hypothesis: Extend the verified 2.65 obstacle planner to quiet safe-zone travel before urgency when the next circle is still beyond the mech. Preserve combat, pickup pursuit and recent-damage response.

Earlier arrival can change exposure and loot timing. The scorer does not publish a per-match breakdown. Test regeneration shelter next and retain urgent-only routing.

experiments.hypothesis: With no engagement or recent warning, scan the least recently observed sector using actual torso facing and the published field of view, reducing the blind interval for initial detection.
experiments.technical_validation: 52 tests; checker 300/300 max 6.7 ms locally. Only aim changed on 39 recorded frames. In 72 stationary open-view cases (24 bearings, three starting yaws, published slew rate), average time until the bearing entered view dropped from 1.783 to 0.381 seconds and maximum from 7.1 to 1.1. Time to sight is a local geometry measure.
experiments.assessment: Rejected against 2.90. The faster open-field scan may spend more time facing irrelevant bearings or change initial engagements. The isolated visibility metric improved but the official aggregate decreased. Retain tracking of confirmed opponents and evaluate defense during weapon downtime.

experiments.hypothesis: While the only gun is reloading against multiple engaged shooters, use the front armor arc to cover more bearings and restore aim before the gun becomes ready. No change to active firing, movement or secondary attacks.
experiments.technical_validation: 55 tests passed. Official checker 300/300 max 6.5 ms locally, no recorded action changes; the starter recording lacks simultaneous opponents. Across eight fixed two-opponent reload scenarios with the official torso turn rate, rear-facing opponent-ticks fell from 200 to 50 and aim returned within floating-point precision when the gun was ready. No inferred match damage or placement.
experiments.assessment: Rejected against the 2.90 parent. The synthetic reduction in rear-facing bearings during reload did not carry through to the official aggregate. Actual opponents move during the reload and a torso turn can give up sensor coverage on the primary opponent. Cause unverified. Evaluate safe starter-drone encounters next.

experiments.hypothesis: Estimate how much recent opponent velocity persists at the current gun travel horizon, using only previously observed motion and a regularized estimate.
experiments.technical_validation: Local diagnostic only. Interpolated observed positions at projectile travel time. First 79 usable forecasts: mean horizontal error 4.025m versus 3.816m for constant velocity; within one radius 30 versus 33. Later 74 forecasts: error 2.141m versus 1.721m; within one radius 52 versus 58. Both segments favored the existing constant-velocity predictor.
experiments.assessment: Rejected locally before integration; keep the existing gun aim. No official evaluation or submission slot used.

No inferred match damage, cube count or placement.
experiments.assessment: Official tie with the selected source. Keep the earlier submission selected. The score does not reveal how many drone encounters occurred. Test preserving existing supply capture progress next.

experiments.hypothesis: Preserve banked progress during the last 1.5 seconds of a supply capture when the observed holder is ourselves, zone travel is safe and known opponents cannot immediately contest the ring. Keep existing combat and safe movement within its boundary.
experiments.technical_validation: 53 tests passed, official checker 300/300 max 7.0 ms locally. The official recording has no supply drops. Six controlled ground scenarios spanning three health values and two initial velocities completed six captures with the constraint versus zero with the parent behavior. This counts boundary crossings and simulated capture progress, not practice results.
experiments.assessment: Promoted by official score at 2.92 versus 2.90. The reported result does not reveal how many late supply finishes occurred. Preserve as the baseline and test laser-cycle positioning separately.

experiments.hypothesis: Pair a reachable firing position with nearby solid shelter while fighting a lone laser-equipped mech. Use a confirmed release to open a brief firing window and return to shelter before the next charge. Avoid permanent cover holding.
experiments.technical_validation: 56 tests, checker 300/300 max 23.5 ms locally, 21 movement changes compared with the 2.92 parent. Supply finish tests and laser cycle tests both passed. The predecessor record includes unchanged local geometry-probe outcomes.

prepared_predecessors.technical_validation: 53 tests, checker 300/300 max 17.5 ms locally. 21 recorded movement decisions changed. All five observed beam releases replayed on approximate ground paths produced one fully sheltered release for both controllers and 110 firing lanes each. In 18 synthetic cycles anchored to recorded poses with a stationary shooter, 11 versus 6 were sheltered at the next release; open firing lanes during the first second were 119 versus 121. Both checks are geometry probes.

experiments.assessment: Official tie against 2.92. Preserve the earlier supply-finish entry. The fixed-source shelter gain failed to increase official placement. The next trial evaluates contact reacquisition independently.

experiments.hypothesis: Orient toward the last reported location of a single confirmed attacking opponent after the engine track expires, while the estimated travel envelope fits in the field of view. Discard confirmed kills and ambiguous tracks, preserve nearer warnings and never fire at an absent opponent.
experiments.technical_validation: 56 tests, checker 300/300 max 6.2 ms locally; 82 recorded aim changes only. For the sole continuously recorded return of contact, the preceding command was 16.8 degrees from the returning bearing versus 140.1 degrees for the parent. A second return followed a 6.4-second observation gap and is excluded from the continuous comparison.
experiments.assessment: Rejected against 2.92. The last-reported bearing matched one recorded reacquisition, but continuing to orient toward stale contacts reduced the official mean. The winning policy retains current engine-provided tracking and resumes its normal behavior when reports end. Test actual geometric isolation next.

experiments.hypothesis: Use balanced mode for a short loaded-gun finishing opportunity with two nearby mechs only when exactly one exposed target can be finished and the other remains screened over sampled reachable approaches. Preserve conservative behavior under active crossfire, low reserves or a third contact.
experiments.technical_validation: 57 tests; checker 300/300 max 6.9 ms locally. No recorded command changes because the kit stream has no simultaneous opponents. In 40 constructed two-opponent configurations on official geometry, the policy relaxed 7 from conservative to balanced. An independently denser approach-angle sweep found no exposed flank in those 7; max complete decision 6.61 ms locally. Geometry and damage timing are estimates, not match outcomes.
experiments.assessment: Official tie. Preserve the selected 2.92 source. The narrow two-opponent finishing geometry changed 7 of 40 constructed decisions, but exposure frequency in the official matches is unavailable. Proceed with the independently validated sloped-ground loot correction.

experiments.hypothesis: Recognize reachable ground-level weapons and cubes across sloping terrain within the existing search radius and zone safeguards. Apply the four-meter pickup-height rule when actually collecting, and continue rejecting inaccessible roof loot.
experiments.technical_validation: 56 tests, checker 300/300 max 7.3 ms locally. No recorded action changes. Of 1,600 deterministic geometry samples (seed 35), 145 had valid ground endpoints differing by at least 4 m. The parent selected none. The candidate selected all 52 with a direct walkable ground route and none of the 93 blocked routes. This is a navigation eligibility result.
experiments.assessment: Official tie. Keep the earlier selected 2.92 entry. Locally the eligibility correction recognized 52 direct ground routes, but its frequency and opportunity costs in practice are undocumented. Evaluate laser release separately.

experiments.hypothesis: Release a fully charged game laser when its actual reported torso ray intersects a clear point on the opponent cylinder, including power-cube size scaling. Preserve the existing charging and retreat rules.

Scenario coverage includes a blocked upper-body intersection and a legal close-range release. This is pose-level release validation.

experiments.hypothesis: Escape a stationary inner-circle hold when flanked by two nearby mechs. Rank feasible exits by nearest opponent clearance and evaluate perpendicular headings. Retain active supply and urgent zone control.

One-step navigation probe on official terrain at the recorded starting pose with 32 rotated diametrically opposed synthetic pairs, 55m away: parent held 31/32 and improved minimum clearance once. multi_step_navigation_probe.method: 16 opposing-pair orientations per condition, 20 decisions at 0.1 s, official terrain and navigation, synthetic instantaneous commanded movement, stationary opponents or both closing at 5 m/s. No damage, acceleration or energy integration. Values are change in distance to nearest opponent, metres.

experiments.interpretation: Deprioritized the sibling pincer intervention after EXP-041 scored 2.56 versus its 2.92 parent. EXP-040 has no official result.

experiments.hypothesis: Avoid reducing the closest flank distance on a candidate navigation step while no projectile needs dodging.
experiments.technical_validation: 54 tests; checker 300/300 with 7.0 ms local maximum. Across 18 feasible synthetic pincer layouts from eight designated map sites and eight orientations per site, two seconds of closing at 5 m/s: mean clearance change was -9.992 m for the selected agent, -3.630 m for EXP-040 and -3.034 m for EXP-041. Worst cases were -10.000, -18.257 and -9.860 m. At the original recorded pose the 16-orientation closing mean regressed from -2.103 to -3.342 m versus EXP-040. Opponent pursuit ignored obstacles; no damage or official placement measured.

ground_acceleration_probe.design: Same 18 feasible paired layouts and closing speed as the cross-map test. Integrate commanded ground velocity subject to published acceleration, reject unwalkable steps, track boost drain and delayed energy regeneration. Opponent paths remain synthetic and ignore obstacles. Two seconds per layout; no weapons, damage or scoring.
ground_acceleration_probe.decision: Prefer EXP-041 for first official evaluation of pincer escape because the larger downside in EXP-040 persisted with acceleration. Use official results to decide whether its sibling warrants a slot.
